proposals.proposal: Write and queue one new blog post targeting the Money Worship pattern. The angle: someone who ties their self-worth to their earning number so tightly that a good month feels like proof they are a good person, and a bad month feels like evidence they are not. Keep it grounded in the specific arithmetic of that feeling rather than abstract coaching language. Title and opening paragraph below.
proposals.new_text:
---
title: "Why does a good income month feel like proof I'm finally a good person?"
pubDate: 2026-06-21
description: "If a strong sales week makes you feel calm and a slow one makes you feel worthless, that's not a budgeting problem. It's worth looking at what the number is actually doing for you."
tags: [money-worship, behavioural-money, self-worth]
---

There's a version of this that sounds like ambition. You hit your income target and something in your chest settles. You miss it and the week feels thin, even if nothing material has changed — the rent is still covered, the fridge is still full.

Joel sees this in clients who earn well and feel fine precisely when the number is climbing. Not because they're greedy. Because somewhere along the way, the monthly total became a read-out on whether they were okay as a person.

That's a lot of weight to put on a figure in a spreadsheet.

The honest reckoning here isn't about earning less or wanting less. It's about noticing what you're actually asking the number to tell you — and whether it has ever, once, told you anything that stayed true for longer than a fortnight.
